sections.heading: FAQs About Asphalt Shingle Roof Repair in West Orange and Essex County

faqs.q: What is the difference between 3-tab and architectural shingles for a West Orange home?

runs.v: Architectural shingles bond multiple fiberglass-mat layers into a dimensional profile that lasts about 30 years and rates up to 130 mph; 3-tab is a single flat layer that lasts about 20 years and rates near 60 mph.

faqs.q: How long do asphalt shingles last on a West Orange home?

runs.v: Architectural shingles last about 30 years and 3-tab about 20, per InterNACHI and the NRCA, with actual life varying up to 40% with climate, installation, and attic ventilation.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for asphalt shingle roofing in West Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Re-covering a detached one- or two-family house is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit. Other buildings need a permit once work exceeds 25% of the roof in 12 months, as do structural repairs and new construction; confirm with the West Orange construction office before work.

faqs.q: Does a West Orange historic landmark need extra approval for an asphalt re-roof?

runs.v: It can. A locally designated landmark or a property in a historic district can need extra review before exterior work, so confirm with the West Orange construction office first. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: Can asphalt shingles withstand the wind on the First Watchung ridge in West Orange?

runs.v: Yes, when a West Orange roof is rated and installed correctly: architectural shingles rate up to 130 mph with the 6-nail pattern, above the 58 mph gust threshold NOAA sets for a severe thunderstorm.
